item.title: Long Enough To Earn A Table Of Contents
item.description: Headings are third-party text as well, and the rail they land in is 150px wide.
item.dc:creator: Overflow Author
item.content:encoded:
An ordinary paragraph, here so the measurement can tell an overflowing line apart from an article box that has been inflated to the width of its widest unbreakable thing. If the article inflates, this paragraph is laid out wider than the viewport too, and the reader has to pan sideways to finish every line of it.

This post exists to be TALL. PostBody only builds a table of contents for an article at least two viewports high with at least one h2 in it, so every other body in this fixture is measured with the left rail empty — which is exactly how a heading rendered outside the article went unmeasured. The paragraphs below are filler with one job: get past that threshold at 1200px, where the two-column grid is live and the rail is a fixed 150px track.

An ordinary paragraph, here so the measurement can tell an overflowing line apart from an article box that has been inflated to the width of its widest unbreakable thing. If the article inflates, this paragraph is laid out wider than the viewport too, and the reader has to pan sideways to finish every line of it.

Why dangerouslySetInnerHTML is fine here

The first heading is ordinary newsletter prose with one long word in it — no pasted secret, nothing anybody would call hostile. A word that does not fit a 150px rail is enough on its own: the entry lays out at its own min-content width and paints over the opening paragraphs of the article beside it.
